location.section: ch. 1; ground name read in the local e-text (Vaidya)

paraphrase: Pramuditā (Joyful): The bodhisattva who has produced the thought of awakening enters the first ground, is joyful at being born into the Tathāgata's family, is freed from five fears (of livelihood, disrepute, death, bad destinies, assemblies) and makes ten great vows; the perfection of giving predominates.

location.section: ch. 10; ground name read in the local e-text (Vaidya)

paraphrase: Dharmameghā (Cloud of Dharma): He is consecrated by the rays of all buddhas as a great lord of the dharma and rains the dharma on beings like a cloud; the perfection of knowledge predominates.
notes: Passage located and read in the local e-text (see location.section); paraphrase by U39 (skeleton phase, fidelity not yet checked).

location.section: ch. 2; ground name read in the local e-text (Vaidya)

paraphrase: Vimalā (Stainless): The bodhisattva keeps the ten wholesome paths of action purely, even in their subtle forms; the perfection of morality predominates.
notes: Passage located and read in the local e-text (see location.section); paraphrase by U39 (skeleton phase, fidelity not yet checked).

location.section: ch. 3; ground name read in the local e-text (Vaidya)

paraphrase: Prabhākarī (Luminous): Seeing all conditioned things as impermanent and burning, he attains the four dhyānas, four formless attainments, immeasurables and superknowledges; the perfection of patience predominates.
notes: Passage located and read in the local e-text (see location.section); paraphrase by U39 (skeleton phase, fidelity not yet checked).

location.section: ch. 4; ground name read in the local e-text (Vaidya)

paraphrase: Arciṣmatī (Radiant): He cultivates the thirty-seven wings of awakening; views of self are burned away; the perfection of vigour predominates.
notes: Passage located and read in the local e-text (see location.section); paraphrase by U39 (skeleton phase, fidelity not yet checked).

location.section: ch. 5; ground name read in the local e-text (Vaidya)

paraphrase: Sudurjayā (Hard to Conquer): He understands the four noble truths and the two truths in all their forms and, for beings' sake, masters worldly arts and sciences; the perfection of meditation predominates.
notes: Passage located and read in the local e-text (see location.section); paraphrase by U39 (skeleton phase, fidelity not yet checked).

paraphrase: Abhimukhī (Facing): examining dependent origination in all its forms, the bodhisattva realizes: 'this triple world is mind only; even the twelve links of existence taught by the Tathāgata all rest on mind'; the three doors of liberation appear before him; the perfection of wisdom predominates; he has keen conforming patience but not yet the acceptance of non-arising.

location.section: ch. 7; ground name read in the local e-text (Vaidya)

paraphrase: Dūraṅgamā (Far-Going): He practices skillful means, entering cessation moment by moment without realizing it, living in the world while beyond it; the perfection of skillful means predominates.
notes: Passage located and read in the local e-text (see location.section); paraphrase by U39 (skeleton phase, fidelity not yet checked).

paraphrase: Acalā (Immovable): the bodhisattva attains the acceptance of the non-arising of dharmas and effortless, non-conceptual knowledge, as one waking from a dream of crossing a river drops all effort; about to rest in that peace, he is roused by the buddhas to remember his vows and beings, and so continues; the perfection of vow predominates; he is never apart from seeing buddhas.
notes: Passage located and read in the local e-text (see location.section); paraphrase by U39 (skeleton phase, fidelity not yet checked).

location.section: ch. 9; ground name read in the local e-text (Vaidya)

paraphrase: Sādhumatī (Good Intelligence): He knows beings' minds, faculties and defilements perfectly and teaches with the four analytical knowledges (pratisaṃvid); the perfection of power predominates.
